facts: Manufacturer states SP3T On-On-On, top actuation, straight PC terminals, break-before-make.
Listing showed zero stock; price is not an availability guarantee.
Terminal spacing code D (0.100 in): single row 1-2-3 at 2.54 mm, 3-4 at 5.08 mm; recommended PCB hole (0.8) dia; terminal section (0.4) x (0.6) mm.

Body (15.8) x (4.0) mm, (4.5) mm high; terminals (3.0) mm below body per H48 ((3.4) in H47 isometric; conflict unresolved); actuator (1.2) x (1.5) mm protruding (2.0) mm above body; (2.0) mm travel per step. Actuator top about 6.5 mm above PCB (derived). All reference dims, no tolerances.
Terminal 3 lies on the body and actuator centreline (centre marks, not toleranced). Four corner standoff bosses on the underside; no PCB mounting pegs.
Contact material is silver, not gold: the NKK product page's General Specifications table states "Contact Finish: Silver Plating" (source range-contact-finish).

NKK Electrical Ratings page Z33 (source range-z33) defines Low Level / dry circuits as <=0.4 VA at <=28 V AC or DC max, and recommends gold-plated contacts there because no arc forms to break down tarnish; it recommends silver for Power Level (~100 mA-10 A @125 V AC), stating an arc only develops above about 12 VDC / 0.5 A, which is what keeps a silver contact's oxidation cleaned off. The companion operating-range page (source range-operating-range) restates the same gold-for-dry-circuit recommendation.

Actual sense path (scripts/make_design.py ~47-49): switch COMMON -> 1 k-ohm -> 100 nF -> mux/buffer. For a full 0<->3.3 V throw: initial capacitor current = 3.3 V / 1 k-ohm = 3.3 mA; RC time constant tau = 1 k-ohm x 100 nF = 100 microseconds. Current then decays to leakage/input-bias current; the centre throw additionally sources through the R40/R41 divider, about 5 k-ohm source impedance. There is no continuous wetting current. The manufacturer's 100 mA / 30 V maximum rating is a ceiling, not evidence that this near-zero-current dry circuit is a suitable application for a silver contact.
open_questions: STOP: pad geometry and 2 mm lever/panel access are not qualified; numeric terminal map resolved from NKK catalogue H46/H47, still needs a drawn footprint and real-part fit check.

OPEN: terminal 2/3 (M/C) mapping is a vendor fact (C->3 is COM, M->2); terminal 1/4 (L/H) follows NKK Left/Right naming but the panel-legend direction is a layout decision, not yet confirmed. Swap to L->4 / H->1 if the panel reads the other way at layout.

OPEN_REQUIRES_MANUFACTURER_CONFIRMATION_AND_QUALIFICATION (#27/#38): SS14MDP2's silver contacts sit in a near-zero-current dry sense circuit (3.3 mA initial transient decaying in ~100 us to leakage/bias current, no continuous wetting current) that NKK's own page Z33 describes as the case gold contacts are recommended for. Not substituted under the decided option (#27 option 2): keep SS14MDP2, do not invent a substitute MPN. Before this switch is approved for this application: get NKK's specific confirmation for this exact load, and run application-level qualification (contact-resistance measurement at the actual load, a cycling/durability run, and an environmental/cleaning exposure check per the factory process) beyond initial continuity. See design/evidence/range-contact.md. A maintained break-before-make SP3T with manufacturer-supported dry-circuit (e.g. gold) contacts remains a listed OPEN alternative, not a decision -- any real substitute needs its own exact pin map, footprint, actuator-height and factory-process review.
Cleaning process not process sealed (hand clean locally, NKK H44); price/lead time via RFQ.
